messages.subject: lavaan verbose output
parts:
When I run the 3-factor Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example with verbose = TRUE, lavaan prints 37 values of the objective function and reports the following.

"
number of iterations:  35
number of function evaluations [objective, gradient]:  36 36
"

I am trying to understand why these numbers differ from one another.

The last two values of the objective function seem consistently equal.  So, I am guessing that lavaan evaluates the function for the first 36 of the 37 printed values, but that the final line simply repeats the value from the prior evaluation without re-evaluating.  Thus the number of evaluations is one less than the number of values printed.

I am further guessing that iterations refer to parameter value updates that take place between the first 36 printed values, the first value being based on the start values.  Thus, there are 35 iterations between the fist 36 values (and no iteration between the last two values).

Am I interpreting that correctly?

Keith Markus

On 09/25/2016 05:52 PM, kmarkus via lavaan wrote:
> When I run the 3-factor Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example with
> verbose = TRUE, lavaan prints 37 values of the objective function and
> reports the following.
>
> "
> number of iterations: 35
> number of function evaluations [objective, gradient]: 36 36
> "
>
> I am trying to understand why these numbers differ from one another.
>
> The last two values of the objective function seem consistently equal.
> So, I am guessing that lavaan evaluates the function for the first 36 of
> the 37 printed values, but that the final line simply repeats the value
> from the prior evaluation without re-evaluating. Thus the number of
> evaluations is one less than the number of values printed.

That is correct. lavaan needs one additional function evaluation, after
the optimizer finishes.

> I am further guessing that iterations refer to parameter value updates
> that take place between the first 36 printed values, the first value
> being based on the start values. Thus, there are 35 iterations between
> the fist 36 values (and no iteration between the last two values).

No. Depending on many factors, only a single function evaluation may be
needed per iteration, or many more function evaluations may be needed
for a single iteration. For example, the political democracy example:

example(sem)
fit <- sem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, verbose = TRUE)

needs 78 function evaluations, over 66 iterations.

To see the iterations themselves (instead of just the function
evaluations), you can switch on the 'trace' option of the nlminb optimizer:

fit <- sem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, control = list(trace = 1))

Now, you see only the 'iterations'. To see both function evaluations and
iterations, use:

fit <- sem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, verbose = TRUE, control =
list(trace = 1))

and you will notice that in particular at the beginning, two, sometimes
three function evaluations are needed per iteration.

Yves.
